correctness.summary: The proof reduces real degree-two harmonics to traceless symmetric quadratic forms, computes their second and fourth spherical moments exactly through Gaussian radial factorization, solves the resulting zero-sum fourth-power eigenvalue optimization with a complete equality analysis, and extends the sharp result to complex harmonics by phase averaging. Exceptional dimensions n=2 and n=3 and the equality conditions were checked separately.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The historical Stanton-Weinstein problem and its local-maximizer follow-up were checked, together with later reverse-Holder and asymptotic spherical-harmonic literature and searches under degree-two, traceless-quadratic, matrix-moment and exact-constant formulations. No source located stated the exact all-dimensional degree-two constant or its complete complex equality classification. Duoandikoetxea (1987) remains the main residual risk because its full theorem text was not inspected, and an invariant-theory or matrix-moment equivalent may exist under different notation.

value.summary: The theorem gives an exact finite-degree reverse-Holder constant in every dimension, classifies all extremizers, and completely determines the degree-two case of the classical global L4/L2 extremal problem on S^2. The traceless-matrix formulation is also reusable for low-degree spherical moment inequalities.

limitations: The theorem is exact only for degree two and does not determine the global extremal problem for arbitrary harmonic degree.
Duoandikoetxea (1987) is a material residual originality risk because its full theorem text was not inspected.
An equivalent statement may exist under invariant-theory, matrix-moment, quadratic-form, or differently notated reverse-Holder literature.
Independent audit has not been performed.
